exercises.name: Lateral Lunge

source_english.description: The bodyweight lateral lunge steps one foot sideways, bends that knee while the other leg stays long, then pushes back to center.
instructions: Stand tall with feet together or hip-width apart and brace the trunk.
Step to one side and bend that knee while pushing the hips back.
Keep the opposite leg long and the planted foot flat.
Push through the bent leg to return to standing, then switch sides.
form_cues: Keep the stepping knee over the toes.
common_mistakes: Rolling onto the inside edge of the foot.
source_english.safety_note: Use a shorter step if balance or hip mobility limits a stable return.

exercises.name: Lateral Squat

source_english.description: A lateral squat shifts the hips to one side into a squat while the opposite leg remains more extended.
instructions: Stand in a wide stance with toes slightly turned out and brace your core.
Shift your hips to one side and bend that knee while keeping the other leg long.
Keep the bent foot flat and the chest lifted.
Push through the bent leg to return to center, then repeat on the other side.
form_cues: Keep the knee tracking with the toes.
Send the hips back and sideways.
source_english.safety_note: Use a stance width that lets you keep both feet planted and the spine controlled.

exercises.name: Reverse Lunge

source_english.description: The bodyweight reverse lunge steps one foot backward, lowers both knees, then pushes through the front foot to stand.
instructions: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart and brace your core.
Step one foot backward and lower both knees toward a comfortable lunge depth.
Keep the front foot flat and the torso upright.
Push through the front foot to return, then alternate legs.
form_cues: Track the front knee over the foot.
common_mistakes: Letting the front knee cave inward.
Pushing off the rear toes instead of the front foot.
source_english.safety_note: Use a stable support nearby if balance is limited and keep the step length comfortable.

exercises.name: Sumo Squat

source_english.description: A bodyweight sumo squat uses a wide stance and toes turned out as the hips lower between the knees.

Descend until the thighs reach a comfortable depth with the knees tracking the toes.
Drive through both feet to stand tall without bringing the feet together.

source_english.safety_note: Use a depth that lets the feet stay flat and the knees track smoothly.

exercises.name: Single Leg Glute Bridge

source_english.description: Lie on the back with one foot planted and the other leg straight, lift the hips, lower them, then switch legs.
instructions: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the ground.
Extend one leg straight out in front of you.
Engage your glutes and lift your hips off the ground, forming a straight line from your knees to your shoulders.
Hold for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your hips back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch legs.
common_mistakes: Using momentum instead of the target joint path.
source_english.safety_note: Keep the bench stable and stop if the pelvis cannot stay level.

exercises.name: Lying Knee Raise

source_english.description: A lying knee raise draws both bent knees toward the torso while the abdomen controls the pelvis against the floor.
instructions: Lie on your back with legs extended and arms beside you or lightly braced.
Brace your abdominals and bend both knees.
Lift the knees toward the chest by curling the pelvis gently upward.
Lower the feet toward the floor without arching the lower back, then repeat.
form_cues: Move the pelvis, not just the thighs.
common_mistakes: Flattening the movement into a hip flexor lift.
source_english.safety_note: Use a smaller range if the back lifts from the floor.

instructions: Start in a high plank position with your hands directly under your shoulders and your body in a straight line.
Engage your core and lift your right hand off the ground, reaching across to tap your left shoulder.
Place your right hand back on the ground and repeat with your left hand tapping your right shoulder.
Continue alternating shoulder taps while keeping your hips and torso stable.
